references.text: The prophecy that the Messiah committed no violence and had no deceit in his mouth confirms Jesus' claim that no one can convict him of sin.
David's prayer to be freed from hidden sins and innocent of great transgressions reflects Jesus' total innocence, which he challenges his opponents to prove.
Job challenges God with the question of who can justify themselves, a question Jesus turns around by challenging people to find any sin in him.
Jesus previously states that whoever speaks the truth seeks honor from God, not from men, which is the basis for his claim that he speaks the truth.
Jesus identifies himself as the truth, giving authority to his question of why they do not believe in him when he speaks the truth.
Jesus confirms to Pilate that he was born to testify to the truth, and that everyone who is of the truth hears his voice, which connects to his challenge to believe in him.
